title: Incident Bot v2 Kickoff Notes (Incident context + diagnostics improvements)
content:
Incident Bot v2 — Kickoff Notes
Date: 2025-02-11
Facilitator/PM: Talia Benson
Doc owner: Talia Benson (SRE Program)

Why we’re here
We keep losing time in the first 5–15 minutes of incidents because responders have to manually piece together (a) what changed, (b) what config/routing changed (and whether it’s tenant-safe to share), and (c) whether the platform is saturated / capacity constrained. This project upgrades incident-bot to automatically attach a standard “first 5 minutes” context payload in #incidents and #eng-oncall.

Scope reminder (agreed)
In-scope
- Slack incident-bot v2 experience: context “cards”, interactive actions (expand diff / open dashboards), retries/timeouts, feature-flag rollout.
- Backend endpoints/services needed to provide deploy metadata, config diffs with redaction, telemetry aggregation with caching/guardrails.
- Observability: saturation metrics standardization, dashboards, and alert tuning aligned to SLOs/error budgets.
- Runbooks/standards for incident context collection and access/audit requirements.
Out of scope
- Full incident management process overhaul
- Major status page/tooling changes
- Data warehouse re-architecture

Attendees (kickoff)
SRE / Incident Response
- Sean Gallagher (exec sponsor) — not present, async approval
- Rafael Mendes (delivery lead)
- Miles Thornton (incident automation)
- Aisha Bello (SLOs/alerting)
- Jacob Stein (diagnostics)
Platform / Control Plane / Routing
- Priya Natarajan (platform sponsor)
- Ethan Park (control plane lead)
- Mina Haddad (routing lead) — partial
Telemetry / Observability
- Logan Wright (telemetry platform lead)
- Allison Grant (observability standards)
Release Engineering
- Connor O’Brien (release eng)
Product
- Marissa Cole (product lead)
Security / Compliance
- Naomi Feldman (security/compliance advisor)

Working agenda
1) Quick context: recent incidents + recurring “context gaps”
2) What “good” looks like: required cards + minimum payload
3) Top incident classes to target (prioritized)
4) Data sources + permissions model (what the bot can call)
5) Success metrics + measurement plan (beta vs GA)
6) Risks/constraints (redaction, audit, query budgets)
7) Decisions needed this week + owners

1) Recent incidents / context gaps (examples mentioned)
- Hosted API 503s (deploy regression): responders didn’t have recent deploy timeline + canary status in thread; manual queries + lots of “what changed?” messages.
- Streaming timeouts: difficulty correlating to deploy/config changes; lacking quick saturation indicators (queue depth/KV cache pressure).
- EU-West capacity saturation: responders needed consistent GPU + scheduler saturation signals and current routing/fallback policy in one place.

Common gaps (compiled)
- No authoritative “recent deploys” view per service/region in thread (including rollout phase and canary health).
- Config changes are hard to find quickly; unsafe to paste raw diffs into Slack.
- Saturation is debated using inconsistent signals; GPU util alone is noisy.
- Telemetry queries during incidents can be slow/expensive; the bot must not become load.

2) What good looks like: v2 cards (initial proposal)
Card A — Recent Deploys
- Service + region context
- Most recent deploy(s): version/image SHA, deploy start time, rollout phase (canary/staged/full), canary signal summary (pass/fail/unknown)
- Link to rollout UI + link to PR/commit(s)

Card B — Customer/Tenant-safe Config Diff
- Diff summary: changed fields + “risk flags” (routing policy, model pin, quotas, feature flags)
- Redaction: secrets removed; only allowlisted keys; show “N redacted fields” with explanation
- Interaction: “Expand diff” opens modal (still redacted)
- Link to source-of-truth config UI (auth-gated)

Card C — Saturation Signals
- GPU utilization (pool-level), queue depth, scheduler/backpressure indicators, KV cache pressure
- Highlights/threshold badges (“High”, “Critical”) with minimal explanation
- Links to dashboards and traces
- Note: must degrade gracefully; if query fails => show cached values + links

Card D — Error budget burn links (nice-to-have, but SRE wants early)
- Per service/route/region burn-rate link(s)
- Lightweight “are we burning?” indicator to align triage to SLO impact

Minimum viable “first 5 minutes payload” (draft)
- incident_id / channel / timestamp
- service, region, environment
- deploy_context: last_deploy_id, last_deploy_time, rollout_phase, canary_status
- config_context: diff_present(bool), diff_summary, redaction_count
- saturation_context: gpu_util, queue_depth, kv_pressure, backpressure
- deep_links: dashboards, logs/traces, rollout, config UI

3) Top incident classes (prioritized)
Priority 0 (address in beta)
- Deploy regressions causing elevated 5xx/503 or latency spikes
- Misconfig/routing policy changes causing 5xx, misroutes, or sudden capacity imbalance
- Regional capacity/saturation incidents (GPU pool saturation, scheduler queueing/backpressure)
Priority 1 (follow-up)
- Streaming disconnects/timeouts (correlation to deploy, saturation, or upstream instability)
- Tenant-specific issues (quota/rate limit spikes, model pin incompatibility)
Priority 2 (later)
- Provider dependency issues (upstream auth, cloud outages) — bot should still help via status + fast links, but not primary focus

4) Data sources + permissioning (initial alignment)
Deploy metadata
- Source: release/event stream or internal deploy registry
- Needed fields: service mapping, region, image SHA, rollout phase, canary outcome, PR links
- Owner: Connor O’Brien + Sahana Iyer (release eng)

Config diff
- Source: config service diff endpoint (tenant-aware)
- Must-have: strict allowlist, secret detection, and “safe rendering” format
- Owner: Ethan Park + Benji Okafor (platform), with review by Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin (security)

Telemetry/saturation
- Source: telemetry query service (metrics + traces) with caching and query budgets
- Must-have: bounded cardinality, rate limiting, circuit breaker, and caching across repeated interactions
- Owner: Logan Wright + Nadia Rahman (telemetry), with Jacob Stein (diagnostics)

Permissions + audit logging
- Bot service identity with least-privilege scopes (deploy/config/telemetry)
- Break-glass flow for Sev0/Sev1 where needed (audited)
- Audit events emitted on privileged operations (who/what/when/why)
- Owner: Kaitlyn Nguyen (authn/authz) + Kevin Osei (audit logging/SIEM)

5) Success metrics + measurement plan (initial)
Primary outcome metrics
- MTTR reduction (overall + by incident class)
- Time-to-triage (time from incident open to first grounded hypothesis / mitigation path)
- Repeat incident reduction (proxy: fewer “unknown cause” postmortems; fewer repeated misconfig incidents)

Leading indicators (beta instrumentation)
- “Context completeness score” per incident thread (did we populate deploy/config/saturation cards?)
- Bot response time p50/p95 for initial context render and interactive actions
- Telemetry query cost/budget adherence (requests/min, cache hit rate, timeouts)
- On-call satisfaction: lightweight survey after rotation (2–3 questions)

Baseline + targets (draft numbers to validate)
- Target: 15–25% MTTR improvement for top 3 incident classes by end of quarter
- Target: 80%+ context completeness for incidents where service+region can be determined
- Target: bot context render within 10–15 seconds p95 (with degraded mode if upstream slow)

Measurement plan
- Beta cohort: SRE rotation only + limited regions/services
- Compare pre/post within same incident classes; also track “first 5 minute” message volume reduction (“what changed?” type messages)
- Add structured log event when bot posts context (include completeness + timing)

6) Constraints / risks (captured)
- Tenant/customer data handling: no secrets or sensitive config in Slack; strict redaction and allowlists.
- Partial outages: bot must continue to be useful when telemetry/config services are degraded (timeouts + cached output + links).
- Query/cardinality cost: diagnostics must not amplify incidents; rate limits + caching + circuit breakers are required.
- Slack interaction constraints: ack deadlines and idempotency; pagination for large diffs.
- Human factors: cards must be concise; avoid “wall of text”. Truncation rules + strong deep links.

7) Decisions needed this week (and where)
Decision 1: Required fields for “v2 beta payload” (to unblock schema + endpoints)
- Proposed owner: Miles Thornton + Jacob Stein
- Review: Rafael Mendes + Allison Grant
- Target: end of week

Decision 2: Config diff allowlist + redaction policy v1
- Proposed owner: Ethan Park + Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Security review: Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin
- Target: end of week (draft), next week (approval)

Decision 3: Saturation signals standard set + thresholds for highlighting
- Proposed owner: Logan Wright + Allison Grant
- Input: Ravi Menon + Mina Haddad (routing/graceful degradation)
- Target: next week

Decision 4: Rollout plan + feature-flag cohorts + rollback criteria
- Proposed owner: Rafael Mendes + Marissa Cole
- Target: next week

Action items (initial)
- Talia: create project tracker doc + weekly sync cadence; compile links to prior incidents + top gaps (Due: 2025-02-13)
- Miles: draft Slack card layout and interaction flow (expand, links, retries) + initial payload schema notes (Due: 2025-02-14)
- Connor: provide sample deploy metadata export payload + service/region join approach (Due: 2025-02-14)
- Ethan: outline config diff endpoint API shape + auth model; identify redaction hooks (Due: 2025-02-14)
- Logan: propose telemetry query budget defaults + caching strategy; list candidate saturation metrics (Due: 2025-02-14)
- Allison: define initial thresholds + dashboard link format requirements (Due: 2025-02-18)
- Naomi: identify compliance/audit requirements for bot access + retention expectations (Due: 2025-02-18)

Open questions (parking lot)
- How do we determine service/region reliably from an incident thread (manual command vs automatic inference)?
- What is the canonical mapping between deploys and affected routes/models (especially for shared components)?
- Config diff edge cases: partial propagation, rollback churn, multi-tenant overlays — how do we summarize safely without misleading responders?
- Saturation: what do we show when signals disagree (GPU low but queue high)? What’s the bot’s “explain like I’m oncall” hint?
- Deep links: what’s the required URL parameter set to land on the right service/region/time window in Console?
- Break-glass: what constitutes a Sev0/Sev1 trigger for elevated access, and how do we avoid normalizing it?

Notes to self (PM)
- Keep beta scope tight; aim for “3 cards + links + degraded mode” rather than full parity across all envs.
- Ensure we instrument completeness and latency from day 1; otherwise we won’t be able to prove impact.
- Make sure Support/CS has a path to consume output or request context for customer escalations (likely later phase).

Next meetings
- Working session: Payload schema + required fields (Miles/Jacob/Allison/Logan) — 2025-02-13
- Security review: Redaction + audit model (Ethan/Kaitlyn/Naomi/Kevin) — 2025-02-14
- Release/Deploy metadata review (Connor/Sahana/Miles) — 2025-02-14

Appendix: Proposed Linear breakdown (for tracking)
- ENG-5421 Recent deploys card
- ENG-5422 Config diff fetcher + redaction
- ENG-5423 Saturation signals card
- ENG-5425 Slack interactive actions ack/retry
- ENG-5426 Permissioning + scopes
- ENG-5427 Telemetry query cache/coalescing
- ENG-5428 Feature-flag rollout

End of notes
